Content warning

This site covers the killings of women in Ekurhuleni, Gauteng, in 2026, and gender-based violence. The women were real people who died recently, and their families are grieving. Descriptions are brief, factual and non-graphic. The site has no crime-scene images and does not embed photos of the victims.

If you need support, or have information:

  • GBV Command Centre (24/7): 0800 428 428
  • Lifeline South Africa: 0861 322 322
  • Anyone with information: SAPS Crime Stop 08600 10111 or the MySAPS app. In an emergency, call 10111.

This is an active police investigation. Police have not confirmed that the deaths are linked or that one person is responsible. This site does not name persons of interest or suspects, and anyone who has been charged is presumed innocent.

      Text version: case summary, case files and full timeline

      Content warning: killings of women and gender-based violence. Descriptions are factual and non-graphic. Help: GBV Command Centre 0800 428 428 · Lifeline 0861 322 322. Information: SAPS Crime Stop 08600 10111 or the MySAPS app.

      Summary (as of 30 September 2026)

      From July 2026, the bodies of a series of women were found in the City of Ekurhuleni, Gauteng, South Africa, mostly in and around Kempton Park, the R21 corridor, Olifantsfontein/Clayville and Tembisa, with others in KwaThema, Springs and Dawn Park (Boksburg). SAPS set up a dedicated multidisciplinary task team on 14 September 2026. On 29 September President Cyril Ramaphosa said 11 women's bodies had been found in Ekurhuleni since July and that the investigation had been raised to national level. Police have not confirmed a serial killer. The President said: "At present, the police have not found evidence establishing that these killings were committed by a single perpetrator. All possibilities remain under investigation." Arrests have been made in three cases. Police cite relationship motives in two of them and have not linked those to the others. In a third, a man has been charged with murder; police said it was too early to say whether it is linked. A twelfth death, a shooting in Tembisa on 28 September, is not part of the task team cases. A woman found in Soweto (outside Ekurhuleni) on 20 September has been mentioned by police, but no link has been confirmed. People charged are presumed innocent and are not named here, and persons of interest are not named.

      Case files (13)

      1. Busisiwe Mahlangu (37)

        Status: arrest made (partner; not linked to other deaths per police)

        Last seen: not reported
        Body found: 15 Jul 2026: Open field (veld) near the R21, Kempton Park (approximate location as reported; map pin at road/area level)

        Found naked with her hands bound with cable ties (as reported by BBC and IOL). She was the first of the women whose deaths are now part of the Ekurhuleni investigation.

        Investigation / court: Her partner (boyfriend) was arrested two days later, on 17 July 2026, and remains in custody (BBC, Presidency). The accused has not been named here; he is presumed innocent. No court date was found in public reporting.

        Link status: Arrest made: her partner (per police). Police say he has not been linked to the other deaths.

        Sources: Ekurhuleni killings: What we know after bodies of 12 women found in South Africa (BBC News, 2026-09-28); After another woman murdered in Ekurhuleni, here's what we know about the killings (Daily Maverick, 2026-09-28); Address to the nation by President Cyril Ramaphosa on the killings of women in Ekurhuleni and the national response to gender-based violence (The Presidency, 2026-09-29); Ekurhuleni women's deaths: Latest shooting not linked as cemetery suspect arrested (IOL, 2026-09-28)

      Patterns & differences (as stated by officials and experts; no conclusion drawn)

      • SAPS (14 Sept statement): The similarities between cases were 'sufficiently concerning for the police to issue a public warning'.
      • Prof Gérard Labuschagne, former SAPS profiler (16 Sept): 'Due to the relatively close geographic proximity and timeframe of the murders and the similar victimology, it makes sense to treat this as a serial (murder investigation) until information to the contrary comes to light.' He said he was not involved in the investigation.
      • Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia (20 Sept): '…not confirmed conclusively that we are dealing with a serial killer because all the cases are not necessarily linked. There are some indications of different modus operandi and different motives.'
      • Gauteng Commissioner Lt Gen Tommy Mthombeni (23 and 26 Sept): 'As of now, we could not confirm whether there is a serial killer, though it cannot be ruled out.' On 26 Sept he referred to a 'similar victimology' and modus operandi among earlier cases.
      • President Cyril Ramaphosa (29 Sept): 'At present, the police have not found evidence establishing that these killings were committed by a single perpetrator. All possibilities remain under investigation.'
      • Forensic specialist quoted anonymously by Daily Maverick: Offenders can change their methods, so differences between cases don't rule out a link; but South Africa's high crime rates mean that cases in the same area could be unrelated.
      • Similarity reported: Victims reported as black women, mostly in their 20s and 30s.
      • Similarity reported: Most bodies were found in and around Kempton Park, the R21 corridor, Clayville/Olifantsfontein and Tembisa; several were near the R21.
      • Similarity reported: Six bodies were found within about ten days in September, mostly in open or secluded places, with no eyewitnesses identified publicly.
      • Similarity reported: Several victims were reported as found partially clothed or unclothed.
      • Difference reported: Three cases have arrests, and police cite relationship motives in two of them (Mahlangu: partner arrested; Ntimba: 'love triangle' per police). A 12th case (Nhlanzi) involved an estranged husband as a person of interest, and police say it is not linked.
      • Difference reported: Reported causes of death differ: stab wounds, a throat injury, strangulation, head injuries, and a shooting.
      • Difference reported: Dawn Park (Boksburg), KwaThema and Springs are further from the Kempton Park cluster; the Soweto case is outside Ekurhuleni.
      • Difference reported: One victim (Mathebula) had been missing since March 2026, with ransom demands reported. Others were found within days of last being seen.

      Where sources disagree

      • How many cases? The President (29 Sept) said 11 bodies had been found in Ekurhuleni since July. BBC (28 Sept) counts 12, including Boitumelo Nhlanzi, whom police say is not linked. Daily Maverick (28 Sept) lists 13 victims, including the Soweto case and Nhlanzi. Earlier reports gave 5, 8, 9 and 10 as cases were added or found.
      • How many were reported missing first? The President said 'only two' of the women had been reported missing. Daily Maverick says at least four had been reported missing before they were found.
      • Arrests in the Ntimba case Most reports: three arrested, two women charged, one man released. BBC (26 Sept) says 'three men appeared in court' in one of the earlier cases.
      • Nxumalo arrest timing Saturday evening, 26 Sept (Daily Maverick) vs Sunday morning, 27 Sept (Presidency).
      • Mjobo date 26 Aug (BBC, SAPS list) vs a 24 Aug case near the R21 mentioned by IOL/The Star, which may or may not be the same case.
      • Names and spellings Ntimba / 'Timba' (eNCA); Ntombifuthi / 'Ntombifuthu' (IOL); Boitumelo Nhlanzi / 'Boitumelo Gift Mashita' (BBC); Villa Liza / Villa Lisa; Olifantsfontein / 'Olifantsfontain' (BBC).
      • Mapping errors elsewhere At least one outlet and one published map placed Gracious Nkomo in Dawn Park, apparently confusing her with Jabulile Ntimba. This site follows SAPS/SAnews, BBC and Daily Maverick.

      Precinct crime context (SAPS)

      Figures cover a whole police station precinct (all murders reported there), not the exact place where a body was found. The precinct is the one that contains each approximate map pin. Near a precinct border, the case may fall under the neighbouring station. Sum of the four SAPS quarterly releases for 2025/26 (each quarter taken from its own release). SAPS quarterly figures can be revised in later releases, so this may differ slightly from an annual report. Population: Stats SA Census 2022 per police district (as compiled in afrith/crime-stats). Rates use 2022 population with 2025/26 counts, so they are indicative only. Precincts with business districts, industry or transport hubs (e.g. Germiston, Primrose, Kempton Park) have many daytime visitors but few residents, so rates per resident can look high there.

      • Kempton Park: 29 murders in FY 2025/26, 4 in Apr–Jun 2026, ≈43.5 per 100,000 (Census 2022 population 66,629).
      • Olifantsfontein: 5 murders in FY 2025/26, 2 in Apr–Jun 2026, ≈13.8 per 100,000 (Census 2022 population 36,196).
      • Kwa Thema: 29 murders in FY 2025/26, 4 in Apr–Jun 2026, ≈22.2 per 100,000 (Census 2022 population 130,892).
      • Dawn Park: 75 murders in FY 2025/26, 27 in Apr–Jun 2026, ≈52.8 per 100,000 (Census 2022 population 141,917).
      • Moroka: 107 murders in FY 2025/26, 19 in Apr–Jun 2026, ≈43.2 per 100,000 (Census 2022 population 247,551).
      • Tembisa South: 76 murders in FY 2025/26, 26 in Apr–Jun 2026, ≈44.3 per 100,000 (Census 2022 population 171,458).
      • Springs: 58 murders in FY 2025/26, 14 in Apr–Jun 2026, ≈44.0 per 100,000 (Census 2022 population 131,838).
      • Tembisa: 90 murders in FY 2025/26, 22 in Apr–Jun 2026, ≈28.6 per 100,000 (Census 2022 population 314,181).

      Scenario views (HYPOTHETICAL)

      The interactive map includes two hypothetical geometry views, "single offender" and "more than one offender". Police have NOT established either. They show approximate distances, OSRM driving and walking times, and time gaps between the approximate pins, and they draw no conclusions.

      47. President's address to the nation on the Ekurhuleni killings

        29 Sep 2026, evening · official statement · National (televised address) · Investigation & officials

        President Ramaphosa said the bodies of 11 women had been found in Ekurhuleni since July. The investigation was raised to national level under the Deputy National Commissioner for Detective Services, and the CSIR is helping with digital forensics. He said: 'At present, the police have not found evidence establishing that these killings were committed by a single perpetrator. All possibilities remain under investigation.' He also said forensic material had been collected and persons of interest identified in other cases, and announced national measures including a case-recovery audit, a plan for the forensic backlog, municipal women's safety audits and alcohol-related measures.

        Evening address; the exact start time is not given in the transcript.

        Sources: Address to the nation by President Cyril Ramaphosa on the killings of women in Ekurhuleni and the national response to gender-based violence (The Presidency, 2026-09-29); Specialised team probing Ekurhuleni murders (eNCA, 2026-09-30)

      48. Accused in Nxumalo case appears in court; bail hearing postponed

        29 Sep 2026 · court / charges · Tembisa Magistrates' Court · Ntombifuthi Nxumalo

        The man appeared in the Tembisa Magistrates' Court charged with murder. The State opposes bail; the hearing was postponed to 6 October and he remains in custody.

        Sources: Ekurhuleni murder accused to remain in custody as bail date postponed (TimesLIVE, 2026-09-29)

      About this case map & method

      Purpose & neutrality

      This is a neutral, source-cited reference about the deaths of women whose bodies were found in the City of Ekurhuleni (Gauteng) from July 2026. It is compiled only from public police and government statements and from news reports. It draws no conclusions about whether the cases are connected. As of 30 September 2026, police had not established that the killings were committed by a single perpetrator. The President said: "All possibilities remain under investigation."

      Labels

      • police statement SAPS statements and on-record police comments, as reported.
      • official statement Presidency, ministers, Parliament.
      • court / charges court appearances and charges, as reported.
      • media report facts reported by the media that are not directly attributed to police.
      • expert opinion views of named or anonymous experts; these are opinions.
      • scheduled future court dates as scheduled on 30 Sept; outcomes are not known here.

      Case status wording

      • under task team investigation part of the police investigation; no arrest reported.
      • arrest made someone has been arrested or charged. Police describe the Mahlangu and Ntimba cases as having separate (relationship) motives. For the Nxumalo case, police said it was too early to say whether it is linked.
      • not part of task team cases / outside Ekurhuleni police say it is not linked, or it happened outside the metro.

      Naming and privacy

      • Victims are named only as publicly released by police or major media. Unidentified women are described by place and date.
      • Persons of interest and uncharged suspects are never named. Accused people are described, not named, even when some outlets name them, and they are presumed innocent.
      • No crime-scene images or victim photos, and no home addresses. Map pins sit at suburb or road level, labelled "approximate location of where body was found as reported".

      Get help / give information

      • GBV Command Centre (24/7): 0800 428 428
      • SAPS Crime Stop: 08600 10111 · MySAPS app · emergency 10111
      • Lifeline South Africa: 0861 322 322

      Map method

      • Pins were placed by geocoding the reported suburb, road or landmark with OpenStreetMap Nominatim, then rounded. The pin precision is shown for each case. Where two cases share an area (R21, Kempton Park), markers are offset slightly.
      • Last-seen markers appear only where a place was reported. Vutomi Mathebula's marker is her stated destination (Dragon City), not a confirmed sighting.
      • Ekurhuleni boundary: geoBoundaries (Municipal Demarcation Board/OCHA), simplified.
      • Background map: Esri's public ArcGIS Online tiles (World Dark Gray Canvas by default; World Street Map and World Imagery in the picker). They need no API key and load from a downloaded copy (file://) as well as online. If a provider keeps failing, the map switches automatically to the next one (Esri mirror host, then Esri street map darkened, then OpenStreetMap on web pages only). OpenStreetMap's own tile server is not the default because it blocks requests from local files.

      Scenario views (HYPOTHETICAL)

      • Neither scenario reflects a police finding. They are geometry exercises showing distances and time gaps between approximate pins. Police have not established either scenario.
      • Single offender: connects the body-found sites in the order they were found. By default it uses the 11 Ekurhuleni cases the President counted, and you can exclude the cases with arrests. Each leg shows the straight-line distance plus OSRM driving and walking route distance and time.
      • More than one offender: the three cases with arrests each form their own group, as police treat them. The Nhlanzi case (police: not linked) and the Soweto case (outside Ekurhuleni) are left out. The remaining cases are grouped by single-linkage clustering: two sites join the same group if they are within D km in a straight line and were found within T days of each other. D and T are shown and can be changed.
      • Timing check: for pairs of cases where a last-seen time and a found time are both reported, the site checks whether the two windows overlap and compares the gap with the drive time. It only reports whether the reported times rule travel in or out.

      Precinct crime context

        Limits

        • Counts differ between sources (9, 10, 11, 12 or 13) depending on the date and on which cases are included. See "Where sources disagree" in Case files.
        • Many times are approximate or not reported. Dates without a reported time are plotted at midday.
        • Things may change quickly: court dates on 1 and 6 October 2026 are after this snapshot.

        Compiled 30 September 2026 (SAST).
